text:
Florentine and Venetian women have fine little mouths and may be procuresses, especially the old; beside Lombards, Romans, Genoese, Piedmontese, and Savoyards, Paris has the finest tongue. Neapolitans are famed for fair speech, they say; Germans and Prussians love cackling; Greek, Egyptian, Hungarian, Spanish, Catalan—Paris has the finest tongue. Bretons, Swiss, Gascons, women of Toulouse: two fishwives on the bridge silence them. Nor Portuguese, English, Calaisiennes, Picards, Valencians—Paris has the finest tongue.

Envoy

Prince, grant Parisian women the prize for speaking well; despite the Italians, Paris has the finest tongue.

Quatrain

I am François, which grieves me, born in Paris near Pontoise, and from a fathom of rope my neck will learn what my arse weighs.


Note: Poem written in prison, when Villon was sentenced to hang.

translation.title: Ballad of the Women of Paris
